preamble: Depalatalization of [ʃ] to [s] involves the movement of the articulation from the post-alveolar to the alveolar region. In Samic, Proto-Uralic *š merged completely with *s (*iša 'skin' > Proto-Samic *ësē), while Finnic took the opposite route to h. Polish mazurzenie is filed under the retroflex cell ʂ → s (cz/sz/ż/dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] > c/s/z/dz), not here.

examples.note: Proto-Baltic turned PIE *ḱ into *ś, 'later merged into *š' (Wikipedia, Proto-Baltic language); Latvian made this *š into s, while Lithuanian keeps š (šimtas).
Smoczyński (1982: 227), as excerpted in the Vilnius University etymological database: Latvian suns < *sunis, which with Lithuanian šuõ and Old Prussian sunis continues Baltic *šu̯ōn- < PIE *k̑u̯ōn-.

examples.note: Reconstructed stage: Proto-Uralic *š merged with *s in Proto-Samic, whereas Finnic turned it into h (Finnish iho 'skin').
